name: Moses of Chorene
summary:
Moses of Chorene (moses-of-chorene) was a prominent Armenian historian from late antiquity and the author of the History of the Armenians. He is considered one of the most important sources on Armenian history during this period.

Born in unknown, Moses of Chorene died in 490 CE. His work provided crucial information about the history of Armenia, its rulers, and cultural developments. This historical account has been invaluable for scholars studying the ancient Near East and the early Christian world.

The significance of Moses of Chorene's work lies in its contribution to our understanding of Armenian identity, the spread of Christianity, and the cultural exchange between Armenia and other civilizations. His writing not only preserved the history of his people but also influenced the development of Armenian literature and culture.

As a historian, Moses of Chorene was part of a larger tradition of Armenian scholars who sought to understand their place within the broader ancient world. His work continues to be studied by scholars today, offering insights into the complexities of identity, culture, and history in late antiquity.

Moses of Chorene's legacy can be seen in the many historical accounts he preserved, including the History of Armenia, which remains an essential source for understanding the region's rich cultural heritage. His contributions to Armenian historiography have had a lasting impact on our understanding of the ancient world and its ongoing relevance today.

In his work, Moses of Chorene wrote: 'The world is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page.' (moses-of-chorene). This quote reflects his commitment to exploring the complexities of human history and culture through extensive research and writing.
